title: Jump Game V
summary: Given an array of integers arr and an integer d, you can jump from index i to index i + x or i - x where 0 arr[j] for all indices j between i and the new index.
statement: Given an array of integers arr and an integer d, you can jump from index i to index i + x or i - x where 0 arr[j] for all indices j between i and the new index. Starting from any index, determine the maximum number of unique indices you can visit without jumping outside the array.
constraints: Start at any index and jump left or right by at most d positions.
A destination must be strictly lower than the current value, and every crossed position must also be lower than the current value.
Return the maximum number of visited indices including the start.
hints: Each valid jump strictly decreases value, so the state graph has no cycle.
Memoize the best path length starting at each index.
Scan outward in both directions up to d, stopping that direction at the first equal-or-higher blocker.
The recurrence tries every legal next index; strict decrease makes cached recursion well-founded.
editorial: Memoized depth-first search returns the longest decreasing path beginning at one index. In each direction, scan only until the distance limit or the first blocking value; positions beyond a blocker are illegal even if lower. Maximize over all starts. The oracle independently enumerates every legal path without memoization on seeded small arrays.

tests.explanation: An optimal decreasing jump sequence visits four indices.
Equal values block every jump, so any path visits only its start.
